content.question: 이번 Intake가 결정할 범위를 무엇으로 확정할까요?

choices.decision: Work Unit lifecycle artifact handoff 계약을 정의한다.
choices.pros: 백업 발생의 근본 원인을 해결하고 범위가 명확하다.
choices.cons: 일반적인 백업 정책은 별도 결정으로 남는다.

choices.decision: 백업 저장 위치와 보존 정책만 정의한다.
choices.cons: 수동 handoff와 불필요한 백업 발생이 계속될 수 있다.

choices.decision: handoff와 Agent Factory 전체 백업 정책을 함께 정의한다.
choices.cons: 범위가 커지고 서로 다른 책임이 결합될 수 있다.

content.recommendationRationale: 직접 원인인 handoff 연결 규칙에 집중하면 불필요한 백업을 줄이고 구현과 검증 범위를 명확하게 유지할 수 있다.

content.question: ready Intake와 실행할 Work Unit을 실행 브랜치에 전달하는 공식 방식은 무엇으로 할까요?

choices.decision: main에 ready Intake와 Work Unit을 checkpoint commit한 후 그 커밋에서 Work Unit branch와 worktree를 생성한다.
choices.pros: Git이 handoff와 복구 기록을 담당하며 미추적 원본, 별도 백업, 추가 handoff 명령이 필요 없다.
choices.cons: 실행 전 lifecycle artifact 커밋이 main 이력에 남는다.

choices.decision: worktree.py handoff 명령으로 미추적 artifact를 Work Unit branch에 전달하고 원본을 승인 후 정리한다.
choices.pros: 코드 변경은 실행 브랜치에만 유지할 수 있다.
choices.cons: 복사, 해시 검증, 실패 복구, 원본 정리와 receipt 계약이 추가되어 복잡하다.

choices.decision: 외부 staging 디렉터리를 표준화하고 그 경로를 거쳐 Work Unit branch로 전달한다.
choices.pros: main을 즉시 clean하게 유지하고 원본 보존이 쉽다.
choices.cons: lifecycle source가 여러 위치에 존재하며 경로, 보존, 정리 문제가 계속된다.

content.recommendationRationale: canonical lifecycle artifact를 ready 시점에 Git checkpoint로 확정하면 handoff를 Git 이력으로 단순화하고 임시 백업과 수동 정리를 제거할 수 있다.

content.question: ready Intake와 ready Work Unit 문서 묶음을 Git에 어떻게 저장할까요?

choices.decision: Intake와 Work Unit을 한 번에 같은 checkpoint commit으로 기록한다.
choices.pros: 두 문서가 항상 한 세트로 남아 원자적인 handoff가 된다.
choices.cons: 일부만 별도로 승인하거나 이력을 구분하기 어렵다.

choices.decision: ready Intake를 먼저 commit하고 ready Work Unit을 나중에 별도 commit한다.
choices.pros: Intake 확정과 Work Unit 생성 이력을 단계별로 구분할 수 있다.
choices.cons: 두 commit 사이에 Intake만 기록된 중간 상태가 존재한다.

choices.decision: 두 문서 외에 당시 변경된 .agent-factory 전체를 함께 commit한다.
choices.pros: 한 번의 commit으로 artifact 변경을 정리할 수 있다.
choices.cons: 관련 없는 작업 파일이 섞일 수 있다.

content.recommendationRationale: Intake와 Work Unit을 한 세트로 기록하면 불완전한 중간 handoff 상태를 피할 수 있다.

content.question: Intake와 Work Unit의 두 checkpoint commit을 실행할 때 Human 승인을 어떻게 받을까요?

choices.decision: full validation 통과 후 별도 질문 없이 자동 commit한다.
choices.pros: 흐름이 빠르고 미추적 파일이 즉시 정리된다.
choices.cons: Agent가 매번 확인하지 않고 main을 변경한다.

choices.decision: Intake commit과 Work Unit commit 전에 각각 Human 승인을 받는다.
choices.pros: 각 단계의 정확한 파일과 commit을 Human이 확인할 수 있다.

choices.decision: 두 commit의 파일과 메시지를 모두 준비한 후 한 번의 Human 승인으로 순서대로 실행한다.
choices.pros: 승인 횟수를 줄이면서 두 commit을 분리할 수 있다.
choices.cons: Work Unit 준비 전까지 Intake가 미추적 상태로 남는다.

content.recommendationRationale: main 직접 변경이며 Intake 확정과 Work Unit 준비는 서로 다른 lifecycle 단계이므로 각 단계의 정확한 파일과 commit 메시지에 별도 Human 승인을 받는 것이 명확하다.

content.question: 두 checkpoint commit의 검증·승인 확인·Git 실행을 어느 구성요소가 소유해야 할까요?

choices.pros: 두 단계에 동일한 경로 격리, 검증, 승인, commit receipt 계약을 적용한다.

choices.decision: Intake manager와 Work Unit manager가 각자의 checkpoint 명령을 소유한다.
choices.pros: 각 artifact의 검증과 commit이 가까이 위치한다.
choices.cons: Git 규칙과 승인 처리가 두 manager에 중복된다.

choices.decision: 별도 명령 없이 각 Agent가 승인 후 raw git add와 git commit을 실행한다.
choices.cons: 경로 혼입 방지와 receipt 형식이 호출자마다 달라질 수 있다.

content.recommendationRationale: 두 lifecycle 단계 사이의 공통 handoff를 중앙 명령으로 소유하면 관련 artifact만 stage하는 불변조건과 단계별 Human 승인을 한 곳에서 검증할 수 있다.

content.source: git status --short --branch; git ls-files .agent-factory/intakes/work-unit-artifact-handoff-contract; git check-ignore
findings: main matches origin/main before the Intake mutations.
The work-unit-artifact-handoff-contract Intake package is untracked and is not ignored.
No file from this Intake package is present in the current Git index.
interpretations: A branch created from the current main commit cannot contain this canonical Intake package until the package is committed.
limitations: The inspection establishes current repository state only; it does not define the desired handoff policy.

findings: The lifecycle shared engine owns sectioned artifact JSON mutation and validation commands but exposes no Git checkpoint command.
The Intake and Work Unit managers expose artifact creation, mutation, validation, and transition commands; neither exposes checkpoint commit handoff.
worktree.py exposes prepare, inspect, integrate, and cleanup and requires a base ref resolving to a commit for prepare.
worktree.py does not copy or move untracked lifecycle artifacts into a linked worktree.
interpretations: The selected lifecycle-owned checkpoint contract is absent and requires scoped implementation plus tests and documentation.
The checkpoint command can remain separate from manager-owned JSON serialization and from work-unit-execution branch/worktree mutation.
limitations: Source inspection does not prove the future command interface or receipt fields; those must be defined and verified by the Work Unit.

findings: Intake owns readiness and handoff to work-unit-planner.
work-unit-planner may create a Work Unit only from a fully validated ready Intake and must not create branch or worktree side effects.
work-unit-execution owns named Work Unit branch and worktree side effects after an executable Work Unit exists.
The lifecycle skill is the top-level router across Intake, Work Unit, Execution, and Review.
interpretations: A pre-execution two-checkpoint orchestration is a cross-phase lifecycle concern rather than artifact JSON manager ownership or execution worktree ownership.
limitations: The current documents do not specify checkpoint validation, approval assertions, staged-path isolation, or receipt semantics.

findings: The repository is an existing agent-factory Codex plugin and README defines the bundled Plugin Creator validator as the structural validation command.
The repository marketplace entry points to the remote GitHub main branch rather than the local source directory.
The Plugin Creator local reinstall loop applies only when the marketplace entry points to the local plugin source being edited.
interpretations: The Work Unit should run the plugin validator but should not perform or claim a local marketplace reinstall under the current configuration.
limitations: Publication, marketplace upgrade, and reinstall are outside this Intake scope.

content.method: manager source and active contract inspection
findings: execution-init validates the full package and ready semantics, then rejects any lifecycle status other than ready.
attempt-start transitions a ready Work Unit to working and records the execution attempt.

The active skill contracts require full Work Unit validation before execution but do not explicitly state that an accepted execution request for a ready Work Unit proceeds without re-asking settled decisions.
interpretations: The manager already provides the ready-only hard gate; the lifecycle and execution instructions need an explicit no-reprompt rule at the ready execution boundary.
limitations: Source inspection establishes the current static contract and does not by itself verify future agent behavior.

content.title: Codex persisted goals and automatic continuation
findings: Codex lists goals as a stable feature that enables persisted goals and automatic continuation.
The /goal command keeps an objective attached to the active chat while work continues and supports explicit pause, resume, edit, and clear operations.
The official manual does not state that a goal makes every tool action or process uninterruptible or guarantees terminal success despite host, session, policy, or external-service failures.
limitations: This source establishes Codex product behavior, not an end-to-end distributed execution durability guarantee for Agent Factory Work Units.

content.title: Temporal durable execution recovery contract
findings: Temporal defines durable execution as persisting workflow state so execution resumes from the recorded point after process crashes, network failures, or infrastructure outages.
Failure-prone external work is modeled as retryable Activities while deterministic workflow state is recovered and replayed.
Completion depends on durable state persistence and recovery semantics rather than keeping one worker process continuously alive.
limitations: Temporal is an external orchestration system; its guarantees do not automatically apply to Codex or this repository unless equivalent mechanisms are implemented and verified.

content.title: Azure Durable Task checkpoint, retry, and recovery model
findings: Microsoft documents that Durable Functions manages workflow state, checkpoints, retries, and recovery for long-running workflows.
The reliability guidance distinguishes transient failures, which can be retried, from persistent failures, which remain errors.
Microsoft recommends idempotent operations so retries do not duplicate side effects.
limitations: The documentation supports recoverable execution, not unconditional success when a permanent dependency or invalid input prevents completion.

content.title: AWS retry, idempotency, and terminal failure boundaries
findings: AWS recommends exponential-backoff retries for transient failures and fail-fast handling for non-transient failures.
AWS requires retryable mutating operations to be idempotent because replaying a partially completed operation can otherwise corrupt state.
AWS Step Functions documents that retries are bounded by policy and unresolved or non-retriable errors reach an explicit failure path.
limitations: The source does not define this repository’s state machine; it establishes design constraints that must be translated into Agent Factory requirements and tests.

content.question: Work Unit의 끝까지 진행 보장을 어떤 의미로 확정할까요?

choices.decision: 실행 전에 거절하거나, 시작 후 durable checkpoint·자동 재개·멱등 재시도를 통해 성공 또는 명시적인 복구 불가능 실패 상태까지 진행한다.
choices.pros: 장애 후 이어서 진행할 수 있고 무한 정지나 중복 부작용을 방지한다.
choices.cons: 영구 장애에서는 성공 대신 명시적 자동 실행 종결 상태가 될 수 있다.

choices.decision: 시작한 Work Unit은 성공할 때까지 무제한 재시도하며 실패 종료를 허용하지 않는다.
choices.pros: 문자 그대로 성공할 때까지 계속 시도한다.
choices.cons: 영구 오류 시 무한 실행, 비용 증가, 자원 고착이 발생한다.

choices.decision: 현재 Codex 세션 안에서만 automatic continuation을 보장하고 세션 장애 후 재개는 수동으로 처리한다.
choices.cons: 중간 차단 문제를 근본적으로 해결하지 못한다.

content.recommendationRationale: 사전 거절 또는 시작 후 끝까지 책임지는 목표를 유지하면서 프로세스와 네트워크 장애를 견디고 영구 오류를 숨기지 않는 검증 가능한 계약이다.

content.method: ready validation and lifecycle gate inspection
findings: A ready Work Unit already requires all readiness flags, a review timestamp, no unresolved blocking open item, every profile-required section and content kind, a complete canonical execution context, and an anchored ready Intake basis.
execution-init rejects every lifecycle status other than ready before it creates execution state.

The current lifecycle supports blocked as an explicit automatic-execution stop with a required unresolved blocking open item; blocked can later return to a resumable lifecycle state after the blocker is resolved.
interpretations: The requested initial refusal can be deterministic: full validation and ready semantic validation must complete before worktree preparation, execution-init, attempt-start, or scoped mutation.
A permanent failure can be recorded as blocked with evidence without inventing a new terminal lifecycle status or changing the existing metadata schema.
limitations: Current validation proves structural and recorded semantic completeness; it cannot predict every future external failure or guarantee the substantive quality of an unrecorded requirement.

content.method: source, command parser, file inventory, and existing test inspection
findings: worktree.py prepare validates repository, base commit, derived branch, worktree registration, and path collisions, but it does not resolve or validate a canonical Work Unit package, lifecycle status, readiness flags, required content, execution context, or Intake basis.
The existing prepare success test creates and locks work-unit/wu-001 without creating any Work Unit package, proving the Git side effect boundary accepts a nonexistent package.

work_unit.py execution-init performs full package and ready semantic validation, but it also requires the prepared worktree HEAD, so worktree preparation necessarily precedes this manager gate in the documented workflow.
No skills/lifecycle/assets/scripts/artifact_handoff.py or combined admission-and-prepare command exists.
interpretations: The current initial admission rule is declarative and caller-enforced rather than mechanically atomic at the earliest Git side-effect boundary.
A caller can create a branch and linked worktree for a missing, invalid, incomplete, or non-ready Work Unit by invoking worktree.py prepare directly.
limitations: This analysis covers the repository and matching installed plugin files; it does not inspect an external launcher or proprietary Codex runtime that is not present in the plugin.

content.method: state-contract inspection and temporary-repository behavioral reproduction
findings: execution-state/v1 records lifecycle substate, Git subject, revision, attempt, primary invocation, invocation chain, and archived attempt outcomes; it has no completed-step ledger, pending step, checkpoint payload, retry classification, retry counter or policy, idempotency identity, lease, heartbeat, or recovery owner.
attempt-resume only appends a unique Codex session id to invocationChain; no command discovers an interrupted session or starts a replacement session automatically.
A running Work Unit can transition to blocked after an unresolved blocker is added.

The reproduced blocked Work Unit rejects attempt-resume because status is not working, rejects resolving its blocker while blocked because blocked requires an unresolved blocker, and rejects direct blocked-to-working because generic transition to working is forbidden.

After the reproduced workaround blocked-to-backlog, blocker resolution, and backlog-to-ready, attempt-resume still rejects ready and attempt-start rejects the retained current attempt; the execution cannot resume through the public manager commands.
interpretations: The current manager tracks attempt identity and stale-result binding but does not implement durable step-level execution or automatic continuation.
The current blocked recovery path is a deterministic dead end for an active attempt, contradicting the accepted recoverable blocked contract.
limitations: The reproduction uses the repository test helpers and temporary Git data; it does not simulate host power loss or a remote service outage.

content.source: pytest targeted manager/worktree tests; rg interruption and recovery coverage; plugin manifest and hooks inventory; SHA-256 comparison of repository and installed plugin files
content.method: focused regression execution and configuration inspection
findings: Four focused tests for ready rejection, execution attempt identity and resume history, manager-owned execution state, and worktree prepare passed in 103.30 seconds.
The broader selected suite was interrupted after 8 passing tests in 309.44 seconds because it exceeded the focused analysis time boundary; no failure was observed before interruption.
Existing tests cover required-kind rejection, invalid execution context, attempt identity history, duplicate invocation rejection, worktree collisions, integration replay, and cleanup safety.

No existing test covers automatic session recovery, durable completed-step reconstruction, idempotent replay of a scoped mutation, bounded transient retry, abandoned working detection, or blocked active-attempt recovery.
The plugin contains no hooks.json or Stop hook and its manifest only registers skills; no background scheduler or automatic continuation launcher is present.
SHA-256 hashes for the relevant repository skills and scripts exactly match the installed agent-factory plugin version 0.1.0+codex.20260719040900.
interpretations: The current passing tests establish the existing identity and Git safety contracts but do not establish the requested start-or-durable-completion guarantee.
There is no plugin-local mechanism that automatically invokes attempt-resume after a Codex process or session ends.
limitations: The full regression suite did not complete; conclusions about missing recovery coverage come from exact test-name and source searches plus focused tests, not a complete pass of every unrelated test.
